App Header & Sidebar

These strings appear in the left sidebar (landscape) or top toolbar (portrait/tablet mode). The sidebar contains: language selector, region view buttons (Cervical, Thoracolumbar, Lumbar, Whole Spine), Plan/Construct editing toggle, tool palette (Implants, Annotations, Tools), action buttons (Copy Plan, Confirm Plan, Load, Save, PDF, Help, New Patient), session privacy toggle, and theme colour swatches. In portrait mode, the sidebar becomes a compact horizontal toolbar with Demographics/Plan/Construct tabs.

The rod placeholder text shows example measurements.

Implant Modal: Screws, Hooks & Bands

Click any pedicle marker (small circle on either side of a vertebra) to open this modal. It has a three-tier visual hierarchy: SCREWS (top, with Monoaxial/Polyaxial/Uniplanar buttons), HOOKS (middle, with 5 hook types: Pedicle, TP Down, TP Up, Supra-laminar, Infra-laminar), and BANDS & OTHERS (bottom, with Band/Wire/Cable). Screws offer three sizing modes: Standard (dropdown), Custom (free text), and No Size. Screws and hooks have an Annotation field (e.g. fenestrated, cortical, revision). Bands/wires/cables have a free-text Description field. Clicking an occupied zone opens the edit modal (not a duplicate).

Cage Modal: Interbody Cages

Click a disc space (gap between vertebrae) on the spine diagram to open this modal. Cage types are grouped by surgical approach: Posterior (PLIF, TLIF), Anterior (ACDF, ALIF), Lateral (XLIF/LLIF, OLIF). Important: ALIF only appears at L4-S1 disc spaces; ACDF only at cervical levels (C2-C7). Switch the Region View to 'Cervical' or 'Lumbar' to access all types. Each cage type shows Side (Left/Right/Bilateral/Midline), Height, Lordosis, Length, and Width fields. At disc levels that support osteotomies (Schwab 1-2), a picker offers Interbody Cage or Osteotomy.

Osteotomy Modal

Schwab 1-2 (Facet, Ponte) are placed at the disc level: click between vertebrae. Schwab 3+ (PSO, VCR, etc.) are placed on the vertebral body: click midline. The dropdown shows two groups: Posterior (Schwab Grades 1-6: Facet release, Ponte, Standard PSO, Extended PSO, VCR, Multi-level VCR) and Anterior (Corpectomy). Each osteotomy type has a label, Schwab grade, and description. VCR, Multi-level VCR, and Corpectomy also show a Reconstruction Cage text field. Correction angle is optional, defaults to empty with placeholder hints showing typical values. Osteotomies render as amber-coloured markers (red is reserved for destructive actions).

Force Modal

Click the left or right edge zone of a vertebral level to open the Force modal. Six force/correction types are shown as clickable buttons: Translate Left, Translate Right, Compression, Distraction, Derotate CW, Derotate CCW. Forces use blue colour scheme (biomechanics convention for corrective vectors). Forces can only be placed on the Plan. On the Construct tab they appear read-only. Force zones always open the ForceModal regardless of which tool is selected.

Note Modal

Select the Note tool from the sidebar, then click anywhere on the spine diagram. The modal shows preset chips (last visible rib, end-vertebra, apex, transitional level, stable vertebra, neutral vertebra), a free-text field, and a 'Show arrow' checkbox. Preset labels use sentence case.

Inventory Panel

The inventory summary appears below each spine diagram in the Plan and Construct columns. Add implants, cages, and osteotomies to the diagram to see the inventory category headers and item labels. The Rods section appears at the bottom. Demographics panel shows Plan inventory by default with a 'View Final' / 'View Plan' toggle. Rod left/right use 'L:' and 'R:' prefixes. Cage inventory items are labelled by type (TLIF Cage, PLIF Cage, ACDF Cage, etc.).

Linked Screens (Sync)

Open the app in two windows of the same browser on a dual-screen setup. Changes sync automatically via BroadcastChannel. One screen can show the Plan while the other shows Demographics with live inventory. A green link icon in the sidebar indicates active sync. These strings are the tooltip text for the sync status indicator.

Help Modal

Click the Help button (? icon) in the sidebar Actions section. The help modal has multiple sections: Session Privacy, Screws & Hooks, Interbody Cages, Osteotomies, Confirm Plan, Portrait & Tablet Mode, Save/Load/Export, Linked Screens, and Keyboard Shortcuts. Bodies may contain HTML markup. Please preserve any HTML tags (<strong>, <br>, <ul>, <li>, etc.) and only translate the text content. The help modal uses a two-column layout in landscape and closes with Escape.
help.about_button
About Skeletal Plan
help.artificial_discs.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Click on a disc space and choose <strong>Artificial Disc</strong>. Cervical disc replacement (ACDR) systems (M6-C, prodisc C, Mobi-C, Bryan, Synergy) are level-aware (C3-C7). Lumbar total disc replacement (TDR) systems (prodisc L, activL, Charité, M6-L, Maverick) span L3-S1. Each disc carries footprint, height, lordosis, and FDA / CE regulatory status.
help.artificial_discs.title
Artificial Discs (ACDR / TDR)
help.barcode.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
<ul><li>Scan with the camera, a handheld USB/Bluetooth scanner, or type the GTIN manually.</li><li>The system, screw type, and size are <strong>auto-filled from the catalogue</strong>.</li><li>Lot number and expiry date are captured for traceability.</li><li>In the implant dialog, the scan card's <strong>Add screw</strong> button records the scanned screw at the level and side it names. On a phone, <strong>↑</strong>, <strong>⇄</strong> and <strong>↓</strong> in the scanner move on with the camera still open.</li><li>A <strong>barcode icon</strong> appears on the chart next to screws with confirmed barcode data.</li></ul>
help.barcode.title
Barcode Scanning (UDI)
help.body_picker.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Click on the body of a vertebra (the midline, not left or right) and a popover offers <strong>Osteotomy</strong> (Schwab 3+: PSO, Extended-PSO, VCR over one or more vertebrae) or <strong>Corpectomy</strong> (body resection + reconstruction cage). Click on a disc space and the popover offers <strong>Artificial Disc</strong> (cervical ACDR or lumbar TDR, depending on level). Each branch is region-aware: only options permitted at that level appear.
help.body_picker.title
Vertebral Body Click
help.bone_graft.body
Record bone graft choices in the demographics panel: Local Bone, Autograft, Allograft, Synthetics, DBM, BMP. Multi-select: combine as needed. Free-text notes capture brand, volume, or harvest-site detail.
help.bone_graft.title
Bone Graft
help.cages.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Click the space <strong>between</strong> vertebrae to place an interbody cage. Six surgical approaches (ACDF, PLIF, TLIF, XLIF, OLIF, ALIF) are filtered by anatomical level. Pick a system from the catalogue or enter dimensions manually. Cages support level moves from inside the modal, but cannot cross between cervical and lumbar regions.
help.cages.title
Interbody Cages
help.case_scan_pool.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Scan implants <strong>before placing them</strong>. Scans not yet linked to an implant collect in <strong>Case scans</strong> on the rail (or in the sidebar). When you place an implant of the matching type, the scan fills in the dialogue and leaves the list. Case scans also holds locking screws and cage anchor screws that are packed separately from the main implant.
help.case_scan_pool.title
Case scans
help.copy_plan.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
When the plan is agreed, choose <strong>Accept plan</strong>. The plan then stays as planned for the rest of the case. If you start the final record first, you are asked whether to accept it. Planned implants not yet on the final record show as faint ghosts on the Final Record (in landscape, when the ghost preference is on). Tapping a ghost offers <strong>Placed as planned</strong>, which records it exactly as planned, <strong>Edit placement</strong>, which opens it pre-filled with the planned size to change before recording, or <strong>Not placed</strong>, which removes the ghost and records that the implant was not used. Before the plan is accepted, <strong>Not placed</strong> asks you to accept the plan first. Undo reverses each. <strong>Mark all as placed</strong> records every remaining planned implant as placed, as planned, and skips any marked not placed. To change an accepted plan, choose <strong>Edit accepted plan</strong>. The edit is recorded in the case and the plan needs accepting again.
help.copy_plan.title
Accepted plan and final record
help.crosslinks.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Place transverse connectors between rods. Select the <strong>crosslink tool</strong> (or press <strong>X</strong>) and click on the chart at the desired level. Crosslinks are anchored to the nearest vertebral level.
help.crosslinks.title
Crosslinks
help.decompression.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Select the <strong>decompression tool</strong> (or press <strong>D</strong>) and click a motion segment to open the overlay. Choose from 13 procedures (laminectomy, laminotomy, foraminotomy, etc.), select <strong>Lee zones</strong> (central, lateral recess, foraminal, extraforaminal) and side (left, right, or bilateral). An MRI-style axial diagram shows the decompression area. Use <strong>Ctrl/Cmd+click</strong> or <strong>Shift+click</strong> to select multiple levels. Duplicate procedures at the same level automatically merge their zones.
help.decompression.title
Decompression
help.desktop_layout.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
On a computer, or a large tablet held landscape, the controls sit on a <strong>rail</strong> down the side. Point at <strong>Add to chart</strong>, <strong>View</strong> or <strong>More actions</strong> to open its panel; click or tap to keep it open. Add to chart holds the tools under Screws, Hooks, Other implants, Procedures, and Notes and marks. The <strong>top bar</strong> holds Undo and Redo, <strong>Accept plan</strong> (on the Final Record, <strong>Mark all as placed</strong>), <strong>Save &amp; Share</strong>, Help, the language and the theme. When the case has previous surgery and the window is too narrow for three charts, a <strong>Previous | Plan</strong> switch in the top bar chooses which is shown beside the Final Record. <strong>Inventory</strong> shows the implant list in place of the second chart, and a <strong>Plan | Final</strong> switch in the top bar (with Previous when the case has previous surgery) chooses the chart beside it. Each chart opens with the whole spine in view. Use the ↕ / ↔ button in a chart's corner to switch every chart between fitting the height and fitting the width; when a chart is wider than its space, drag, or hold Shift and scroll, to move sideways. To take the previous surgery off the case, choose <strong>Remove previous surgery</strong> under More actions (or in the sidebar). You can undo this. For this version, the earlier layout with a sidebar is still available: choose <strong>Classic layout</strong> under More actions, and <strong>New layout</strong> in the sidebar to come back.
help.desktop_layout.title
Desktop layout
help.disclaimer.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
This is a documentation aid for planning and recording spinal implants. It does not choose implants, sizes or levels.<br/><br/>It does not provide clinical decision support, diagnostic information, or treatment recommendations. The <strong>operating surgeon bears full responsibility</strong> for all clinical decisions, including implant selection, placement, and verification at the point of use (WHO Surgical Safety Checklist).<br/><br/>The surgical record produced by this tool is only as accurate as the information entered. The surgeon is responsible for ensuring the record reflects the actual procedure performed.<br/><br/>Patient data remains on the local device and is never transmitted. There is no analytics or telemetry. When you scan an implant barcode, the installable app versions may look that barcode up in a public device database by its number only, never any patient information. The user is responsible for data handling under their local regulations (e.g. GDPR, HIPAA, Caldicott).<br/><br/>This software is provided as-is under a dual licence (Free Clinical Use Licence for clinical planning, teaching, and research; Commercial Licence available for redistribution or commercial integration), with no warranty of any kind. See the bundled LICENSE file for full terms. The developer accepts no liability for clinical outcomes arising from use of this tool.
help.disclaimer.title
Disclaimer
help.encryption.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
The cached case in this browser is encrypted automatically with a 256-bit AES-GCM key. The key is generated once per browser profile and stored in IndexedDB as <strong>non-extractable</strong>: the browser can use it but cannot export the raw bytes. <strong>You don’t enter a passphrase.</strong> The case is therefore only readable in this browser on this device. Uninstalling the browser, clearing site data, or switching to a different browser profile permanently deletes the key and the cached case becomes unrecoverable.
help.encryption.title
Encryption at Rest
help.export_formats.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Export the case as <strong>PDF</strong> (A4 with a clickable case link in the demographics column and the complete case attached, so choosing the PDF with <strong>Open File</strong> reloads it; when the case has scanned implants, their identifiers follow on extra pages) or <strong>.splan</strong> (the full case, which you can open again later). All exports include a translation disclaimer footer when the language is not English. The patient name in the filename can be toggled in Preferences.
help.export_formats.title
Export Formats
help.forces.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Six biomechanical force tools mark corrective vectors on the chart: <strong>translate left/right</strong>, <strong>compress</strong>, <strong>distract</strong>, and <strong>derotate</strong> (clockwise/anticlockwise). Click between vertebrae on the appropriate side to place a force marker.
help.forces.title
Forces & Vectors
help.linked_screens.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Open the app in <strong>two windows of the same browser</strong> on a dual-monitor setup. Use the <strong>Open Second Screen</strong> button for one-click setup. <strong>For best results, rotate your second monitor to portrait</strong>, which gives each column more vertical space and shows the full spine without scrolling. In portrait mode, switch between the <strong>Patient</strong>, <strong>Plan</strong>, <strong>Final</strong>, and <strong>Inventory</strong> tabs. Two landscape monitors work but show the same side-by-side layout on both, so a portrait second screen is the real advantage. Changes sync automatically between windows.
help.linked_screens.title
Linked Screens
help.modular_routing.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Modular screw systems (e.g. Medtronic ModuLeX) ship the shank, head, and locking hardware as separate UDIs. Scan each component and the system routes it to the correct slot in the screw record. If a scan does not match the active screw system or placement type, a <strong>cross-system rejection dialog</strong> warns you before accepting it.
help.modular_routing.title
Modular Systems
help.move_to_level.body
Cages, plates, discs, and screws all support level moves from inside their modal: change the level pickers and the placement re-anchors without losing scan or annotation data. Cross-region moves (cervical ↔ lumbar) are blocked for plates, cages, and discs to prevent accidental anatomical errors.
help.move_to_level.title
Move to Level
help.notes.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Add free-text labels to the chart. Select the <strong>note tool</strong> (or press <strong>N</strong>) and click on the chart. Notes support line breaks and can be repositioned by dragging.
help.notes.title
Notes
help.offline_use.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
This app works best online for automatic updates. For use without internet, <a href="https://github.com/nigelgummerson/spine/releases/latest" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="underline hover:text-slate-800">download the standalone version</a>.
help.offline_use.title
Offline Use
help.osteotomies.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Click on the <strong>vertebral body</strong> (midline) and choose <strong>Osteotomy</strong> for posterior procedures (Schwab 3+: PSO, Extended-PSO, VCR) or <strong>Corpectomy</strong> for anterior body resection. Schwab 1–2 (Facet, Ponte) are placed at the disc level: click between vertebrae. For a VCR, choose the lowest vertebra resected under <strong>Resected down to</strong>: one vertebra is recorded as a VCR, two or more as an ML-VCR, and the chart shows every resected body. A VCR then asks for its reconstruction cage, which shares its levels; changing the levels in either dialog changes both. Corpectomy opens the Reconstruction Cage flow with a structured catalogue picker. Recording a Schwab 3 to 6 osteotomy on the Plan or Final Record removes the screws, hooks, bands, wires and cables at the vertebrae it resects, and none can be added there; scanned implants are removed only after you confirm.
help.osteotomies.title
Osteotomies
help.plates.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Place plates spanning multiple levels: <strong>anterior cervical</strong>, <strong>ALIF</strong>, <strong>lateral</strong>, or <strong>posterior occipital</strong>. Choose cephalad and caudal endpoints: per-region max-span limits are enforced (anterior cervical 5, ALIF 3, lateral 2). Plates can be UDI-scanned to auto-fill the system, length, hole count, and locking-screw fixation.
help.plates.title
Spinal Plates
help.population_ranges
Published pedicle measurements in adults, for reference only. They are not used to set sizes. Catalogue warnings (amber) indicate a selected size is not manufactured in the chosen screw system. This tool documents, records, and communicates the surgeon's plan. It does not check values against patient anatomy.
help.portrait_mode.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
The app detects screen orientation automatically. <strong>Landscape</strong> on a larger screen shows Plan and Final Record side by side, with the controls on a rail (see Desktop layout) or in a sidebar. <strong>Portrait</strong> shows one column at a time with a control rail along the side. Tap the tabs (or swipe) to switch between <strong>Patient</strong>, <strong>Plan</strong>, <strong>Final</strong>, and <strong>Inventory</strong>. Tools, Case scan, region View, Mark all as placed, and a <strong>Save &amp; Share</strong> menu sit on the rail; less-used actions live under <strong>More</strong>. Works on phones and tablets alike.
help.portrait_mode.title
Portrait & Tablet Mode
help.preferences.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Open Preferences under <strong>More actions</strong>, with the gear icon in the sidebar, or with the <strong>,</strong> shortcut. Four tabs:<br/><strong>Privacy</strong>: whether the patient name appears in exported filenames. Save on this device is set at startup and with its switch under More actions or in the sidebar.<br/><strong>Implant</strong>: whether modals auto-advance to the next level after Confirm, and whether system labels appear on chart placements.<br/><strong>Scan</strong>: audio and haptic feedback on a successful UDI scan, and which side of the screen the camera preview floats on.<br/><strong>Manufacturer</strong>: Stryker / VB Spine preference during the labeler transition (click the active button to clear it).
help.preferences.title
Preferences
help.qr.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Use the <strong>QR Image</strong> button under <strong>Save &amp; Share</strong> (or in the sidebar) to download a standalone PNG of the case as a QR code, or <strong>Show QR</strong> to display it on screen for someone to scan with a phone camera. PDF exports embed a clickable case link instead of a QR code.
help.qr.title
QR Code Export
help.qr_code
The QR carries a copy of the case with patient details removed (no patient name, DOB, ID, or surgeon). Notes, annotations and lot numbers are kept as written. It is not encrypted: anyone who scans it can read it. A scanned plan must be independently verified before surgical use.
help.quickadd.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Place bilateral pedicle screws across a range of levels in one step. Select your <strong>Upper Instrumented Vertebra (UIV)</strong> and <strong>Lower Instrumented Vertebra (LIV)</strong>, choose a screw type, and confirm. Choose one size for every screw, or leave them unsized and choose sizes in the Plan view or at surgery. A level whose system does not make that size gets an unsized screw. Trajectories and individual adjustments are made in the Plan view. Press <strong>Q</strong> to open.
help.quickadd.title
Quick Add
help.recon_cages.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Click on a vertebral body and choose <strong>Corpectomy</strong>: the procedure that removes one or more vertebral bodies. Pick the cephalad and caudal ends of the resection (up to four vertebrae). The reconstruction cage (a vertebral body replacement, or VBR) spans from the lower endplate of the vertebra above the resection to the upper endplate of the vertebra below it. The catalogue picker covers DePuy Synthes, Globus Medical, Medtronic, Stryker, and VB Spine systems with structured size matrices; coverage is expanding. Other manufacturers can be entered manually.
help.recon_cages.title
Reconstruction Cages (Corpectomy / VBR)
help.report_problem.body
If you find a bug, a data problem or anything that could affect clinical safety, please tell us. Report a problem opens an email with the app version already filled in. Please do not include patient details.
help.report_problem.button
Report a problem
help.report_problem.title
Report a Problem
help.reset_tour.body
Show the guided tour again.
help.reset_tour.button
Reset tour
help.reset_tour.title
Onboarding Tour
help.resetting.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Three separate actions for tidying or finalising a case:<br/><strong>Clear Final Record</strong>: wipes the post-operative Final Record column only. The Plan column is preserved. Use after a planning rehearsal to start the final record again.<br/><strong>Finalise &amp; Lock Record</strong>: locks the entire case for editing. Placements and demographics become read-only and a “locked” stamp appears on exports. Click again to unlock.<br/><strong>New Patient</strong>: wipes everything (plan, final record, demographics, scans). The disclaimer is shown again. Use between cases on a shared workstation.
help.resetting.title
Resetting & Locking
help.revision.body
Plan a revision: open the saved record of the earlier operation and choose Plan a revision. Its implants and procedures are shown as previous surgery, in grey under an empty Plan and Final record, and are not counted as new implants. Notes and markers come across too; forces do not. Scans from the earlier operation are not carried over. A new implant in the same position replaces the old one. To take out an old implant without replacing it, open the dialog at its position: on the Plan, mark it to be removed (red line and REMOVE label); on the Final record, mark it removed (REMOVED on the Previous chart). Rods from previous surgery are shown on the Previous chart only, and are marked to be removed or removed there.
help.revision.title
Plan a revision
help.rods.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Record rod details in the demographics panel: material, diameter, profile, contour, and length for each side. <strong>Linked lengths</strong> keep left and right rods matched. Press <strong>R</strong> to open the rod modal directly. Bone graft is recorded as checkboxes (Local Bone, Autograft, Allograft, Synthetics, DBM, BMP) with optional free-text notes.
help.rods.title
Rods & Bone Graft
help.save_load.body
Save exports a .splan project file that can be reloaded later. PDF export produces the clinical record of the visible chart. The left panel records implant supplier, screw system, bone graft, and auto-generated inventory.
help.save_load.title
Save / Load / Export

Add or update the implant

Chart Navigation

Tools

Views
help.sc.move
Move selection
help.sc.note
Single-letter shortcuts are disabled while typing in a field.
help.sc.rod
Rod
help.sc.save
Save file
help.screws_hooks.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Click <strong>left or right</strong> of a vertebra to open the implant dialog; its title bar shows the level and side it is working on. <strong>Add screw</strong> records the implant and keeps the dialog open. <strong>↑</strong> and <strong>↓</strong> move a level and <strong>⇄</strong> goes to the other side, placing nothing. A level that already has an implant opens with <strong>Update</strong> and <strong>Remove</strong>; Remove keeps the dialog open with the details filled in, so removing and adding again corrects a placement. If you change something and then move or close, the dialog asks before discarding it. The <strong>Bilateral</strong> / <strong>Unilateral</strong> switch sets whether you work on both sides of a level together or one side at a time. A trajectory selector (pedicle, lateral mass, pars, translaminar, cortical) appears at appropriate cervical and lumbar levels. Choose from 3 screw types, 5 hooks, or bands/wires/cables. Turn on <strong>Show Pelvis</strong> under <strong>View</strong>, or press <strong>P</strong>, for S2AI, iliac, and SI-J fixation.
help.screws_hooks.title
Screws & Hooks
help.session_privacy.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Controls whether the case is kept on this device between sessions. <strong>On:</strong> the case is saved here, encrypted, and reloaded next time. It is deleted automatically after <strong>24 hours of inactivity</strong>. <strong>Off (red):</strong> nothing is kept, and anything already stored is cleared. Use Off on a shared or public computer or tablet. Change it at any time with the switch under <strong>More actions</strong>, or in the sidebar. In a web browser you are also asked once at startup.
help.session_privacy.title
Save on this device
help.share_link.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Generate a self-contained URL that encodes the case. Recipients open the link in any modern browser to view the same plan. Typical uses are <strong>pre-briefing implant company reps</strong> so the right kit is staged for theatre, and <strong>discussing cases with colleagues</strong> for second opinion, multidisciplinary review, or teaching. <strong>The link is not encrypted</strong> (anyone with the URL can read it) so treat it like an email attachment. Patient-identifying fields (name, ID, DOB, sex, surgeon, date, location) are stripped before the link is generated; the plan and final record travel in the URL without them. Notes, annotations and lot numbers are kept as written. The encoded data lives in the URL hash fragment, which is never sent to a server.
help.share_link.title
Share Link
help.shortcuts.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
<strong>Dialogs:</strong> <strong>Enter</strong> add or update, <strong>Escape</strong> close (asks before discarding a change), <strong>Delete</strong> remove; Remove keeps the dialog open. <strong>Implant dialog:</strong> <strong>Enter</strong> add, then down a level, <strong>Shift+Enter</strong> add, then up a level; <strong>Alt+↑</strong> / <strong>Alt+↓</strong> up or down a level, <strong>Alt+←</strong> / <strong>Alt+→</strong> other side. <strong>Scroll wheel</strong> over a dropdown, once clicked, to cycle values.<br/><strong>Views:</strong> <strong>C</strong> cervical, <strong>L</strong> lumbar, <strong>T</strong> thoracolumbar, <strong>W</strong> whole spine, <strong>P</strong> pelvis.<br/><strong>Tools:</strong> <strong>I</strong> add to chart, <strong>R</strong> rod, <strong>N</strong> note, <strong>X</strong> crosslink, <strong>U</strong> unstable, <strong>D</strong> decompression, <strong>Q</strong> quick add. Osteotomy, corpectomy, and artificial disc replacement are reached by clicking on the vertebral body or disc space: no keyboard shortcut.<br/><strong>Chart navigation:</strong> <strong>Arrow keys</strong> move a focus ring across vertebrae and zones (left / mid / right); <strong>Enter</strong> or <strong>Space</strong> activates the focused zone (same as clicking it); <strong>Escape</strong> clears the focus.<br/><strong>Actions:</strong> <strong>F</strong> fullscreen, <strong>S</strong> save, <strong>E</strong> export, <strong>,</strong> preferences, <strong>?</strong> help, <strong>Cmd/Ctrl+Z</strong> undo, <strong>Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z</strong> or <strong>Cmd/Ctrl+Y</strong> redo.<br/><strong>Portrait view:</strong> <strong>0–3</strong> (0 Patient, 1 Plan, 2 Final, 3 Inventory) switch tab; swipe between tabs.
help.shortcuts.title
Keyboard Shortcuts

Show Important Notice
help.size_stamp.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
<strong>Drag size</strong> is for quickly laying down screws. The size is always your choice: the app never picks one. Press <strong>Drag size</strong>, beside Quick Add, to turn it on, then choose a head type. <strong>Click</strong> an empty pedicle to add a screw at the last size you placed for that kind of screw (lateral mass, other neck screws, pedicle or pelvic), or unsized if you have not placed one yet; until then, a drag starts from the smallest size. <strong>Press and drag</strong> to set its size: sideways for diameter, up or down for length, in the sizes the system makes. Hold at the edge of the screen to keep stepping the size that way. Let go to add it. Drag an existing screw to change its size. Drag below the shortest length to remove it (the readout turns red and reads Remove), or back up to keep it; Undo brings a removed screw back. Click an existing screw to open its dialog. <strong>Bilateral</strong> works on both sides of a level together. On a phone or tablet, hold for a moment before dragging; a quick swipe still moves the chart. On the final record, a quick tap on a planned screw offers Placed as planned, Edit placement or Not placed; hold and drag to record it at another size. Scanned screws keep their scanned size. Each press is one undo step. Press <strong>Done</strong>, or Escape on a keyboard, to leave. Outside Drag size, a plain click on a pedicle opens the full screw dialog. Use it for what Drag size does not offer: shank and shaft variants, dual diameters, specialist head types (such as reduction, biased-angle or dual-rod heads), the trajectory and annotations.
help.size_stamp.title
Drag size
help.standard_vs_specialist.body
Screw-size pickers default to the standard diameters listed on the manufacturer's Surgical Technique Guide (STG) ordering matrix: these are the sizes hospitals usually stock. Sizes filed under regulatory UDI/GUDID but absent from the STG (half-mm specials, regional or custom-order SKUs) are classified specialist; they still scan, still accept custom-typed values, and remain visible with a leading bullet (•) when already chosen on a placement. Toggle off in Preferences › Implant if your centre carries the wider range.

Standard vs specialist sizes

help.udi_scanning.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Open any implant modal and tap the <strong>scan button</strong>. The camera (or a USB / Bluetooth scanner, or manual GTIN entry) reads the UDI / GTIN / HIBC barcode and auto-fills system, size, lot, and expiry from the bundled catalogue. A <strong>barcode icon</strong> appears beside scanned placements on the chart. Lot and expiry data persist in the saved case file for traceability.
help.udi_scanning.title
UDI / Barcode Scanning
help.unstable.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Mark motion segments as unstable. Select the <strong>unstable tool</strong> (or press <strong>U</strong>) and click between vertebrae. A zigzag marker appears at that level.
help.unstable.title
Unstable Segments
help.vertebral_anatomy.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Most patients have 12 thoracic and 5 lumbar vertebrae. When a patient differs (an extra or missing thoracic level, 4 or 6 lumbar vertebrae, or a lumbosacral transitional vertebra such as a sacralised L5 or lumbarised S1), set it from the anatomy badge in the patient panel. The badge reads <b>Anatomy: Normal</b> by default and turns amber with <b>Anatomical Variation!</b> once a non-standard template is chosen, so a normal patient is never silently planned on an abnormal template. The chosen anatomy is drawn on the chart and stated on the record. Switching anatomy after implants are placed drops any implant on a level that no longer exists, and you are asked to confirm first.
help.vertebral_anatomy.title
Vertebral anatomy
help.view_modes.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Switch between regions with single-key shortcuts: <strong>C</strong> cervical (Occ-T4), <strong>T</strong> thoracolumbar, <strong>L</strong> lumbar (T10-pelvis), <strong>W</strong> whole spine. Toggle pelvis with <strong>P</strong>. The chart auto-fits to whichever range is shown. You can also choose a region from <strong>View</strong>.
help.view_modes.title
View Modes
help.workflow.body Contains HTML: preserve tags
Enter patient details, then build your <strong>Plan</strong> column. Click <strong>left or right of a vertebra</strong> for screws, hooks, or sublaminar fixation. Click <strong>between vertebrae</strong> for cages, plates, osteotomies, or artificial discs. Click on the <strong>vertebral body</strong> (midline) and choose between Osteotomy and Corpectomy. After surgery, switch to the <strong>Final Record</strong> column and confirm or adjust each placement: planned items appear as ghosts until confirmed.
help.workflow.title
Basic Workflow

Common Buttons & Shortcuts

These appear at the bottom of every modal dialog. The four buttons are: Confirm (green), Cancel (grey), Remove (red, only in edit mode), and Close (help/changelog modals). Shortcut tooltips appear on hover. The New Patient action uses a custom confirmation modal (not a browser dialog).

This is a documentation aid for planning and recording spinal implants. It does not choose implants, sizes or levels. The operating surgeon is responsible for all clinical decisions, implant verification, and record accuracy.

This is a documentation aid for planning and recording spinal implants. It does not choose implants, sizes or levels. Surgeon responsible for all clinical decisions and record accuracy.

disclaimer.modal_body Contains HTML: preserve tags
This is a documentation aid for planning and recording spinal implants. It does not choose implants, sizes or levels.<br/><br/>Population-based reference data from published literature may be shown for convenience. These are <strong>group averages from adult studies</strong>, not patient-specific values. The surgeon must verify all data against the individual patient's anatomy and imaging.<br/><br/>The <strong>operating surgeon is responsible</strong> for all clinical decisions, implant verification (WHO Surgical Safety Checklist), and ensuring the record accurately reflects the procedure performed.<br/><br/>Patient data stays on this device. There is no analytics or telemetry, and no patient information is transmitted. The developer accepts no liability for clinical outcomes arising from use of this tool.

modal.quickadd.help
Quick Add places bilateral pedicle screws at every level between your UIV and LIV. Choose one size for every screw, or leave them unsized and choose sizes in the Plan view or at surgery. A level whose system does not make that size gets an unsized screw. To adjust individual levels (remove screws, change type or trajectory, add hooks), use the Plan view. Craniocervical (Oc–C2) and pelvic levels are not included: add these individually.

tip.dual_screen.body
Use the Open Second Screen button in the sidebar, or drag a second browser tab to your other display. Tip: rotate your second monitor to portrait. Portrait mode gives each column more vertical space, showing the full spine without scrolling. You get four tabs: Patient, Plan, Final and Inventory. Two landscape monitors just duplicate the same side-by-side layout.
tip.dual_screen.body_shell
Choose Open Second Screen under More actions, or drag a second browser tab to your other display. Tip: rotate your second monitor to portrait. Portrait mode gives each column more vertical space, showing the full spine without scrolling. You get four tabs: Patient, Plan, Final and Inventory. Two landscape monitors just duplicate the same side-by-side layout.
tip.dual_screen.footnote
After physically rotating your monitor, update your display settings so the computer knows the orientation has changed (System Settings → Displays on Mac, Display Settings on Windows).

Bug Reports

If you notice any technical problems while testing the app in Ελληνικά, please report them here. This could include: layout issues (text overflow, truncation, overlapping elements), broken buttons or interactions, display problems on specific screen sizes or orientations, export/PDF issues, or anything that does not work as expected. You do not need to report English-only issues here. Focus on problems you see when the app is set to Ελληνικά.
